reason: The mini is on nightly and moved itself onto v0.5.0 unattended — verified off the machine today, and the runbook now describes the job it actually runs. Two criteria still need a person at the machine. First, nothing leaves the box when a night goes wrong: the mover writes one line to ~/ergo-fleet/lisa-stay-current.log, and because it compares the installed version before and after, a failed `brew upgrade` logs `current at 0.5.0 on lisa-nightly` — the same words a healthy no-op prints. Second, rollback has never been performed on this box; it was rehearsed on the dev desk, but on Homebrew the way back is `lisa upgrade --tag`, which leaves a second lisa in ~/.local/bin shadowing the formula one, and that interaction is untested here.
ask: On the Mac mini, give it a way to tell you when a night goes wrong, put it back on the previous Lisa once to prove you can, then write both into docs/knowledge/mac-mini-nightly-record.json in this repo.
steps: On the mini, in ~/ergo-fleet/lisa-stay-current: check whether `brew upgrade` actually succeeded instead of inferring it from the version, log `failed` when it did not, and send that line somewhere off the machine (a webhook, a mail command, a push service).
Prove it shouts: make it fail once on purpose (an unreachable brew, a bad formula name) and confirm the message reaches you.
Prove the way back, on the mini: lisa upgrade --tag v0.4.4
Confirm the work still runs under it: lisa --version, then lisa status --path <a board on that box>
Come back: rm ~/.local/bin/lisa && brew upgrade lisa-nightly, and confirm `lisa doctor` reads one lisa at /opt/homebrew/bin/lisa, channel nightly.

Record both in docs/knowledge/mac-mini-nightly-record.json: add data.alert = {"leaves_the_box": "<what you set up>", "tells_failure_from_noop": true}, add data.evidence.rolled_back_here = {"at": "<when>", "from": "<version>", "to": "<tag>", "workloads_ran": "<what you ran and what it said>"}, and drop the data.not_yet_true entries the two steps above have made false.
Run lisa doctor on the mini with PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin — a plain non-login ssh has no Homebrew on PATH and reports a healthy machine as unsupported.
check: python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('docs/knowledge/mac-mini-nightly-record.json'))['data'];a=d.get('alert') or {};r=(d.get('evidence') or {}).get('rolled_back_here') or {};sys.exit(0 if d.get('channel')=='nightly' and a.get('leaves_the_box') and a.get('tells_failure_from_noop') is True and all(r.get(k) for k in ('at','from','to','workloads_ran')) else 1)"
